knowledge:
- key_parameters: outcomes=A matrix of high-dimensional response variables (e.g., gene expression or spectral intensities) ;; design=A data.frame containing experimental design factors ;; formula=A character string specifying the GLM formula (e.g., main effects and interactions) ;; nboot=The number of bootstrap resamples for significance testing (use 100 for quick testing, 1000 for final results) ;; method=The decomposition method to use, either "ASCA", "APCA", or "ASCA-E" ;; combineEffects=A list of character vectors specifying which model terms to combine for joint PCA decomposition ;; drawShapes=A character string specifying shape grouping in score plots, such as "polygon", "ellipse", or "segment"
- alternatives: limma is mentioned as a classical univariate differential expression analysis method, whereas limpca acts as a multivariate complement to visualize global structures.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing high-dimensional -omics datasets (e.g., transcriptomics, metabolomics) from multi-factorial experimental designs (both balanced and unbalanced) to decompose and visualize multivariate structures associated with specific experimental factors and their interactions.
- pitfalls: limpca cannot handle mixed linear models (random effects) directly; users must mean-aggregate hierarchical designs (e.g., aggregating replicates within an aquarium) before modeling. Simple means in plotMeans are biased estimators of expected means for unbalanced designs. High bootstrap counts (nboot) should be avoided during initial code development to save time.

workflows.name: asca_apca_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform GLM-based ASCA, APCA, or ASCA-E analysis on high-dimensional designed data to decompose and visualize multivariate experimental effects.
input: outcomes.tsv (matrix of high-dimensional response variables, e.g., gene expression levels or spectral intensities)
design.tsv (metadata table containing experimental design factors for each sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Format data into an lmpDataList using data2LmpDataList ;; 2. Explore raw data using plotDesign, plotLine, plotScatter, plotScatterM, and plotMeans ;; 3. Perform exploratory PCA using pcaBySvd, pcaScreePlot, and pcaScorePlot ;; 4. Generate the GLM model matrix using lmpModelMatrix ;; 5. Estimate the model and decompose outcomes into effect matrices using lmpEffectMatrices ;; 6. Test effect significance using parametric bootstrap via lmpBootstrapTests ;; 7. Perform PCA decomposition of effect matrices using lmpPcaEffects ;; 8. Calculate and plot contributions using lmpContributions ;; 9. Visualize scores, loadings, and interaction effects using lmpScorePlot, lmpLoading1dPlot, lmpLoading2dPlot, lmpScoreScatterPlotM, and lmpEffectPlot.
workflows.code:
# Data import / formatting
UCH2 <- data2LmpDataList(outcomes = UCH$outcomes, design = UCH$design, formula = UCH$formula)
# Or from SummarizedExperiment
se <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = t(UCH$outcomes)), colData = UCH$design, metadata = list(formula = UCH$formula))
UCH3 <- data2LmpDataList(se, assay_name = "counts")

# Data exploration
plotDesign(design = UCH$design, x = "Hippurate", y = "Citrate", rows = "Time", title = "Design of the UCH dataset")
p1 <- plotLine(Y = UCH$outcomes, title = "H-NMR spectrum", rows = c(3), xlab = "ppm", ylab = "Intensity")
plotScatter(Y = UCH$outcomes, xy = c(453, 369), design = UCH$design, color = "Hippurate", shape = "Citrate")
plotScatterM(Y = UCH$outcomes, cols = c(133, 145, 150, 369, 453), design = UCH$design, varname.colorup = "Hippurate", varname.colordown = "Citrate")
plotMeans(Y = UCH$outcomes, design = UCH$design, cols = c(453), x = c("Citrate"), w = c("Hippurate"), z = c("Time"), ylab = "Intensity", title = c("Mean reponse for main Citrate peak"))

# PCA
ResPCA <- pcaBySvd(UCH$outcomes)
pcaScreePlot(ResPCA, nPC = 6)
pcaScorePlot(resPcaBySvd = ResPCA, axes = c(1, 2), title = "PCA scores plot: PC1 and PC2", design = UCH$design, color = "Hippurate", shape = "Citrate", points_labs_rn = FALSE)
p2 <- pcaLoading1dPlot(resPcaBySvd = ResPCA, axes = c(1, 2), title = "PCA loadings plot UCH", xlab = "ppm", ylab = "Intensity")

# Model estimation and effect matrix decomposition
resLmpModelMatrix <- lmpModelMatrix(UCH)
resLmpEffectMatrices <- lmpEffectMatrices(resLmpModelMatrix)
resLmpEffectMatrices$varPercentagesPlot

# Bootstrap tests
resLmpBootstrapTests <- lmpBootstrapTests(resLmpEffectMatrices = resLmpEffectMatrices, nboot = 100)

# ASCA
resASCA <- lmpPcaEffects(resLmpEffectMatrices = resLmpEffectMatrices, method = "ASCA", combineEffects = list(c("Hippurate", "Time", "Hippurate:Time")))
resLmpContributions <- lmpContributions(resASCA)
resLmpContributions$plotTotal
resLmpContributions$plotContrib

# ASCA Scores and Loadings
all_loadings_pl <- lmpLoading1dPlot(resASCA, effectNames = c("Hippurate", "Citrate", "Time", "Hippurate:Time", "Hippurate+Time+Hippurate:Time", "Residuals"), axes = 1, xlab = "ppm")
hip_scores_pl <- lmpScorePlot(resASCA, effectNames = "Hippurate", color = "Hippurate", shape = "Hippurate")
lmpScoreScatterPlotM(resASCA, PCdim = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2), modelAbbrev = TRUE, varname.colorup = "Citrate", varname.colordown = "Time", varname.pchup = "Hippurate", varname.pchdown = "Time", title = "ASCA scores scatterplot matrix")
lmpLoading2dPlot(resLmpPcaEffects = resASCA, effectNames = c("Hippurate"), axes = c(1, 2), addRownames = TRUE, pl_n = 10)

# Effects plot
lmpEffectPlot(resASCA, effectName = "Hippurate", x = "Hippurate")
lmpEffectPlot(resASCA, effectName = "Hippurate:Time", x = "Hippurate", z = "Time")

# APCA
resAPCA <- lmpPcaEffects(resLmpEffectMatrices = resLmpEffectMatrices, method = "APCA")
lmpScorePlot(resAPCA, effectNames = "Hippurate", color = "Hippurate", shape = "Hippurate", drawShapes = "ellipse")
lmpLoading1dPlot(resAPCA, effectNames = c("Hippurate", "Citrate", "Time", "Hippurate:Time"), axes = 1)

# ASCA-E
resASCAE <- lmpPcaEffects(resLmpEffectMatrices = resLmpEffectMatrices, method = "ASCA-E")
lmpScorePlot(resASCAE, effectNames = "Hippurate", color = "Hippurate", shape = "Hippurate")
